description: A regulatory-grade monitor (OpenAQ isMonitor = true). OpenAQ describes these as the "gold standard" for measuring pollution, typically run by government agencies for regulatory purposes. description: An "air sensor" (OpenAQ isMonitor = false): less sophisticated than a reference monitor, but small, portable and affordable, so institutions and individuals deploy them to fill gaps. In this project: Clarity, AirGradient and BEACO2N devices. Low-cost values pass an outlier rule before use (see "low-cost outlier rule").

name: gina

description: The US EPA's near-real-time air quality network and data feed, the source of all reference-monitor data here (via OpenAQ). Measurements are made by state, local or tribal agencies with EPA-approved reference or equivalent methods. AirNow data get only preliminary quality checks and are not fully validated; EPA's regulatory database, AQS, holds the validated data and replaces AirNow data as it becomes available.
source: AirNow, About the Data (https://www.airnow.gov/about-the-data/), accessed 2026-09-27; Decision OA-D6 caveats

description: Our grouping: sensors of the same type (reference or low-cost), in the same city, within 50 m of each other, chained (A–B and B–C within 50 m → one site). description: One sensor's OpenAQ daily value for one local day: the mean of its hourly values from 01:00 to 00:00 local time, computed by OpenAQ.
source: OpenAQ Docs, Measurements (https://docs.openaq.org/resources/measurements); Step 4
name: gina

description: A sensor-day with at least 18 of 24 hourly values (EPA's completeness rule for a 24-hour PM2.5 average). Sensor-days with fewer hours are not counted.
source: EPA 40 CFR Part 50 Appendix N §3.0(c) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/40/appendix-N_to_part_50); Decision OA-D3
formula_or_derivation: hours_observed ≥ 18
name: gina

description: OpenAQ's "Limits exceeded" marker on an hour outside ~0–1,000 µg/m³. Reference: a negative hour, already left out of the daily value by OpenAQ; flagged reference days are kept. Low-cost: an hour above 1,000 µg/m³ still inside the daily value; flagged low-cost days are removed.
source: OpenAQ /v3/sensors/{id}/flags; Step 5a; Decision OA-D7
name: gina

description: Daily values below 0 (instrument noise in very clean air) are set to 0 before any average; the original value is kept in the audit files.
source: Decision OA-D5
formula_or_derivation: pm25_used = max(value, 0)
name: gina

description: A low-cost sensor-day is removed if it is above 1,000 µg/m³, or above 100 µg/m³ and more than 5 times the city's reference average and/or the median of the city's other low-cost sensors that day (which comparison applies depends on what else was measuring). Reference monitors are not subject to it.
source: Decision OA-D6
formula_or_derivation: see the "rule" row of audit/sensor_day_audit_<city>.csv
name: gina

description: A valid sensor-day that passes all rules (negatives set to 0, not a flagged low-cost day, not a low-cost outlier). Only counted sensor-days enter site and city averages. Each sensor-day's status and reason: audit/sensor_day_audit_<city>.csv.
source: Step 5; Decisions OA-D3, OA-D5, OA-D6, OA-D7
formula_or_derivation: included = 1
name: gina

description: A site's value for one day: the mean of its counted sensor-days that day.
source: Step 5
formula_or_derivation: mean(counted sensor-days at the site)
name: gina

description: The city's value for one day and one sensor type: the mean of that type's site-days in the city, so each site counts once however many sensors it has. Columns ref_mean and lowcost_mean in pm25_<city>_daily.csv.
source: Step 5; Decision OA-D3
formula_or_derivation: mean(site-days of that type)
name: gina

description: The mean of the reference and low-cost city daily means (each type counts 50%); on days with only one type, that type's mean. Column all_mean; all_mean_basis says which applied.
source: Step 5; Decision OA-D3 (option b)
formula_or_derivation: (ref_mean + lowcost_mean) / 2, or the one available
name: gina

description: The lowest and highest site-day value in the city that day: the cleanest and most polluted site. Given per type (ref_min/max, lowcost_min/max) and across both types (all_min/max). Not the lowest or highest hour.
source: Step 5; Decision OA-D3 (option a)
formula_or_derivation: min / max of site-days
name: gina

description: ALA metropolitan area name exactly as listed in the ranking: City1-City2(-City3), State(s). The area is the largest OMB Metropolitan Statistical Area (as of 2023) containing the ranked counties.

description: Metro area's national rank for short-term (24-hour) particle pollution (PM2.5); 1 = most polluted. Blank = not ranked in the short-term list ("—" in the source). Tied metros share a rank.
source: American Lung Association, "State of the Air" 2026 report, About This Report, pp. 7-12; ranks transcribed by Claude from Gina's screenshot of the Most Polluted Cities table
formula_or_derivation: Per county, 2022-2024: weighted total = orange days×1 + red days×1.5 + purple days×2 + maroon days×2.5 (days by 24-hour PM2.5 AQI category); weighted average = total ÷ 3. Metro rank = rank of the highest county weighted average in the metro.

description: Metro area's national rank for year-round (annual) particle pollution (PM2.5); 1 = most polluted. Tied metros share a rank.
source: American Lung Association, "State of the Air" 2026 report, About This Report, pp. 7-12; ranks transcribed by Claude from Gina's screenshot of the Most Polluted Cities table
formula_or_derivation: Metro rank = rank of the highest county annual PM2.5 design value (µg/m³, EPA, 2022-2024) in the metro. A design value is the concentration calculated in the form of the national air quality standard (EPA).
